cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: The Roman army was the most effective military force in the ancient world, enabling Rome's imperial expansion

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: A legion consisted of approximately 5,000-6,000 soldiers divided into ten cohorts

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: Each cohort had six centuries of 80 men commanded by a centurion

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: Legionaries were Roman citizens who served 25 years; auxiliaries were non-citizens who gained citizenship on discharge

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: Roman discipline was legendary — decimation (killing one in ten) punished units that broke ranks

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: Standard equipment: lorica segmentata (armour), gladius (short sword), pilum (javelin), scutum (shield), helmet

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: The Romans built a fortified marching camp every night on campaign for security and routine

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: The testudo (tortoise) formation with overlapping shields protected against missile fire

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: Training was relentless — recruits marched 20 miles in five hours carrying full kit

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: The army was also an engineering force — building roads, bridges, forts and aqueducts

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: The Roman navy (classis) controlled the Mediterranean, securing supply lines

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Roman Army
cards.back: Soldiers were paid, received a pension on retirement and shared in booty from conquests
